body: glTF has no 2x3 matrix type, nor a 6D vector type, so for encoding a Transform2D semantically in glTF, the closest equivalent glTF type is the 3x3 matrix `"type": "MAT3"`, which is 9 floats. As for AABB, it similarly has 6 floats. Technically both of these could be encoded as 6 scalars, which would take up less space, but my assumption is that we want to leverage the existing type semantics in glTF, and glTF often requires padding accessor data. Note that I don't have a use case for AABB, my intention here was to support all Godot Variant types we could reasonably support.
